title: Capability handlers: expose the invocation origin (user input vs timer / task / subscription / effect)

body:
## 最小独立复现

任意一个 `init()` 里调用「已在 `ui/app.toml` 声明」的能力的应用：

```bash
gpui-rhai --root /tmp/repro init
```

`ui/app.toml`:

```toml
entry = "main"
runtime_api = 2

[capabilities]
"app.demo" = "*"
```

`ui/main.rhai`:

```rhai
fn init(ctx) {
    let result = ctx.call_capability("app.demo", "ping", ());
}

fn view(ctx) {
    column([text("hello")]).with_style(style().padding(px(16)))
}
```

```bash
gpui-rhai --root /tmp/repro check
```

## 实际行为

```
gpui-rhai: failed to evaluate Rhai UI source: Runtime error:
capability `CapabilityId("app.demo")` was not declared by the application manifest
```

## 期望行为

`check` 应通过（或以其他方式校验能力声明），因为该应用完全合法：

- 能力契约明确允许同步能力在 `init` 中调用（docs/capabilities.md："Synchronous methods may run only in `init`, `dispose`, or an event callback"）；
- `ui/app.toml` 已声明 `"app.demo" = "*"`；
- 真实挂载路径工作正常：`PreparedScriptView::mount` 会在生命周期启动前执行 `manifest.activate(...)`（crates/gpui-rhai/src/app.rs 两处调用点），同一应用实际运行无此错误。

## 根因分析

`gpui-rhai-cli` 的 `check` 在 `validate_entry`（crates/gpui-rhai-cli/src/lib.rs）中手工搭了一个求值环境：`UiRuntimeState::new()` + `ScriptLifecycle::new(...)`，随后 `lifecycle.start(...)` 会执行 `init`——但全程**没有**把 `ui/app.toml` 里声明的能力激活进 capability registry（`check` 读 app.toml 只校验了 `entry` 与 `runtime_api` 字段）。于是任何在 `init` 或首帧渲染中调用能力的应用都被 `check` 误拒。

这意味着：使用 capability 的应用（docs/capabilities.md 的主推集成方式）全部无法通过 `gpui-rhai check`。

可能的修法方向（供参考）：`validate_entry` 在启动生命周期前，基于 app.toml 的声明做激活；难点在于 check 环境没有真实 handler——可以考虑「声明即放行调用但返回 schema 合法的占位值」，或将该阶段的求值限制为不执行 init 的静态校验。具体语义由你们定。

## 环境

- gpui-rhai 本地 checkout：`0b9b887c`（chore(release): prepare 0.1.8，工作区干净）
- macOS（Apple Silicon）

## 来源与严重度

- 发现场景：Cadenza（真实应用迁移试验田）M1，其 `init()` 需要调 `cadenza.library` 的 `card_status` 加载首屏数据。
- 严重度：**可绕行**（应用真实运行正常，只是 `check` 无法使用；目前跳过 `check`）。

labels.name: cadenza
labels.description: Dogfooding reports from the Cadenza migration (real-app proving ground)

title: gpui-rhai check rejects valid apps whose init() calls a manifest-declared capability

body:
## Context

oh-my-byted lets widgets mark values as openable resources (e.g. a PSM in a "who reads this config" table) and shows an "Open with…" menu on right click. For ordinary nodes, wrapping them in `ContextMenu` works well: `components/menu.rhai` listens to `pointer_down` on the trigger and opens on `event.button == "right"` (`context_request`, 0.1.7).

## Problem

Table builds its row and cell nodes internally (`components/table.rhai`, row renderer). The only pointer hook on a row is `on_click_value(Fn("row_action"))` -> `row_click(key)`; the public events are `sort_change` / `selection_change` / `row_click` / `group_toggle` / `column_resize`. Cells only carry text + adornments, so a caller can't place a `ContextMenu` trigger inside a cell either. Same for Array- and NativeCollection-backed tables.

## Ask

An optional `on_row_context_request` callback. When set, rows get a `pointer_down` handler that, for `button == "right"`, emits:

```rhai
#{ key: <row key>, column: <column key under the pointer>,
   window: #{ x, y } }   // same shape ContextMenu's pointer_open uses for its anchor
```

Left click and keyboard behaviour unchanged. How the caller then shows a menu anchored at that point (a `Menu` with an explicit `anchor`, or a controlled `context_menu` prop on Table itself) is your call.

Nice to have: the context-menu key / Shift+F10 on the focused row emitting the same event with the row bounds as anchor.
title: Table: expose a right-click (context request) on rows/cells so callers can attach a menu

body:
## Context

oh-my-byted hosts script widgets from third-party packages. Per `docs/architecture.md`, Rhai Arrays are for small Table inputs and large inputs should use `NativeCollection`. We hit exactly that boundary: a 1652-row Table scrolled at < 20 fps.

Measured on 0.1.7 (a5876a9), release build, headless `ScriptLifecycle`. One scroll step = shift the requested window by 3 rows and `realize_virtual_requests` 28 rows; median of 40 steps:

| rows | Array: mount | Array: scroll step | NativeCollection: mount | NativeCollection: scroll step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 20 ms | 2.1 ms | 3.2 ms | 1.7 ms |
| 1,652 | 149 ms | 8.3 ms | 3.0 ms | 2.1 ms |
| 3,000 | 401 ms | 13.5 ms | — | — |
| 5,000 | fails: `ErrorDataTooLarge("Size of array/BLOB")` | — | 3.2 ms | 2.0 ms |
| 20,000 | — | — | 3.1 ms | 1.9 ms |

So NativeCollection is clearly the right path. The problem is getting data into it from a generic host.

## Problem

- A collection name must be `register`ed on `UiRuntimeState.native_collections` **before mount** (`ScriptViewExtension::configure_runtime`).
- After mount, the host can only `ScriptViewHandle::replace_native_collection` a name that already exists (`UnknownCollection` otherwise).
- Scripts can only read (`ctx.get_native_collection`).

A host whose widgets decide at runtime what they show therefore needs an out-of-band declaration. oh-my-byted now parses a custom `"omb": { "collections": [...] }` block from each widget's gpui-rhai header, pre-registers empty `<instance>/<name>` collections at mount, and swaps rows in through a host capability and `replace_native_collection` after the script transaction. It works, but every widget author has to declare names up front, and names can't be created on the fly (for example, one collection per opened item).

## Ask (either would let us drop the declaration)

1. A host-side `ScriptViewHandle::register_native_collection(name, collection, cx)`, or let `replace_native_collection` create a missing name.
2. A script-side way to hand an Array to the runtime as a Rust-owned collection, e.g. `ctx.set_native_collection(name, rows, key_field)`, with Rust-owned rows, projection, sort and filter from then on (the one-time Array → collection conversion is fine).

Minor, related: past about 3,000 rows an Array-backed Table fails at mount with `ErrorDataTooLarge("Size of array/BLOB")` from `max_array_size(10_000)` (row items include cell arrays). A message that points to NativeCollection, plus the numbers above in the Table docs, would save the next person the investigation.
title: NativeCollection: allow registering on a live view (or creating one from script), so hosts don't need per-widget pre-declaration

body:
## Symptom

Hosts can test SplitPane keyboard resizing through automation: SplitPane attaches script handlers with `on_key_value("left" / "right" / "up" / "down", ...)`, so `AutomationCommand::Dispatch` of a key event on the separator works. oh-my-byted's GUI selftest drives a SplitPane step this way.

Resizable has no equivalent path. Its keyboard resizing is a GPUI `div().on_key_down` closure inside `ResizableHandlePrimitive` (`resizable.rs:676` on `codex/interaction-runtime-0.1.8`), while `automation_dispatch` (`app.rs:3771`) only walks handlers registered on retained nodes (`dispatch_plan` → Script / Host / Native `UiEventHandler`). Pointer gestures are not dispatchable either, so there is no automation path to resize a Resizable at all. oh-my-byted's floating-window resize is currently covered only by hand.

This comes from reading the code; I have not run a Dispatch against a Resizable handle to see what it returns.

## Ask

Route Resizable keyboard steps through the same retained-handler path SplitPane uses (`on_key_value`, or a `UiEventHandler::Native`), or let automation deliver a real key event to the focused element. Either would make Resizable testable headlessly.

Suggested target: 0.1.9.
title: Resizable keyboard resizing can't be driven by AutomationCommand::Dispatch (native on_key_down), unlike SplitPane

body:
## Symptom

Passing a formal component instance directly as SplitPane `start` / `end` breaks that component's own element ref. In oh-my-byted (0.1.7) a panel cell component declares `element_ref("cell_root")` on its root and reads it when the user floats the cell. Once the cell is passed straight into SplitPane, that fails with:

```
component /View[...]/Cell[cell-clock] has no mounted element ref `cell_root`
```

## Cause

`registry/components/split_pane.rhai` (unchanged on `codex/interaction-runtime-0.1.8`) decorates the caller's node in place:

```rhai
let start = props.start.with_key(start_ref_key)                     // :123
    .with_style(ctx.component_style("start", start_style))
    .with_ref(start_ref)                                             // :125
    .bind_signal(if horizontal { "width_override" } else { "height_override" }, preview);
...
let end = props.end.with_key(props.end_key)                         // :152
```

The collapsed paths (:99, :104) do the same with key and style. A node carries one ref, so the component's root ref is replaced, and its key is rewritten as well.

`Draggable` follows the same pattern for `handle` (`props.handle.with_key(..).with_ref(handle_ref)`); not reproduced there. `Resizable` already wraps `content` in its own `box([...])`.

## Workaround

Wrap each pane before passing it: `start: box([node])`.

## Ask

Have SplitPane (and Draggable's `handle`) wrap the caller's node internally, so the component's key / style / ref / signal land on its own wrapper. Callers cannot tell from the outside that their node will be taken over. Alternatively, document it in the component header.

Suggested target: 0.1.9.
title: SplitPane overwrites key/style/ref on the caller's start/end nodes, breaking formal components passed as panes

body:
## Motivation

Separators are not always a bare line. A common pattern is a 1px line with a centered grip, e.g. shadcn's `ResizableHandle withHandle` (a rounded pill with a 2×3 dot pattern). Today the SplitPane handle *is* `SplitResizePrimitive`, which paints a fixed line itself (`split_resize.rs:195-204` on `codex/interaction-runtime-0.1.8`), so there is nowhere to put such a node. `Resizable` is the same (`resizable.rs:298-308`: edge lines and a 5×5 corner square), and `part_styles.handle` applies one style to every handle.

## Why "just put a node inside the handle" is not enough

A grip is usually wider than the handle (8px by default) and overhangs both panes.

1. **Layout is fine.** `absolute()` plus signed `offset_px` insets work, and overflow is visible by default.
2. **Paint order.** GPUI has no z-index or stacking context; a later sibling paints over an earlier one (gpui 0.2.2 `scene.rs:77-81`). With `[start, handle, end]` (`split_pane.rhai:154`), `end` paints over the grip's overhang wherever it has a background. (shadcn needs `z-10` on the web for the same reason.) Scripts cannot reach `gpui::deferred`.
3. **Hit area.** The primitive's hitbox is its own bounds (`split_resize.rs:167`), so pressing the overhang does not start a drag, and `end`'s hitboxes come later and win `hit_test`.
4. **State.** A grip usually changes look on hover / drag / focus / disabled. That state lives in the primitive and pointer moves don't re-render Rhai; node styles have `hover` / `active` / `focus` for the node itself but no group-hover.

## Proposal

Mirror `Draggable`'s `handle` + `handle_ref` split, where the native primitive owns the gesture and the script node is visual plus an eligible hit region (`draggable.rs:192-196`):

- `handle: optional node` on SplitPane (and a per-handle equivalent on Resizable). Decoration only: keyboard steps, the `separator` role and the tab stop stay on the primitive.
- Paint it above both panes: either the primitive defers the node, or the component renders it as the last child of root, absolutely positioned at the separator and following the native drag preview (that needs a binding that maps the `start-size` preview to a position, not only a size override).
- Pressing anywhere on the node, including the overhang, starts the drag and shows the resize cursor.
- Expose idle / hover / drag / focus / disabled as a native signal the node can bind styles to (precedent: react-resizable-panels' `data-resize-handle-state`), so pointer moves never re-render Rhai.
- Keep the native line as the default when no node is given, with a way to turn it off when the node draws its own line.

Minor, same area: the line's 4px end inset (`px(4.0)` / `px(8.0)` literals) is not configurable. oh-my-byted works around it by stretching the handle along the line, `height(auto()).margin_y(offset_px(-4))`, which makes the line span the full edge with pane geometry unchanged. So a `line_inset` option is nice-to-have, not blocking.

Suggested target: 0.1.9.

Context: oh-my-byted panel grids, where the host turns a grid config into nested SplitPanes.
title: SplitPane: allow a custom handle node (grip) — paint order, hit area and state need native support

body:
## Objective

Consolidate the existing gesture, native-preview, geometry, capture, lifecycle and collection mechanisms before adding more interaction components. ADR 0022 is the authoritative architecture; PR #81 is the implementation branch.

## Foundation

- [ ] characterize existing Resizable, SplitPane, Table resize, Slider, ScrollArea and Chart behavior
- [ ] replace repeated primitive prop readers with one typed PrimitiveContext boundary
- [ ] add atomic PreviewPatch / batched native signal writes
- [ ] add Host-domain GestureSession ownership and one move/up/cancel router
- [ ] add shared Affine2D and presented forward/inverse geometry
- [ ] add stable flat-order/outline projection for virtualized sorting and Tree
- [ ] migrate every existing interaction before shipping new components

## Public components

- [ ] Draggable
- [ ] DragSource
- [ ] DropZone
- [ ] Sortable
- [ ] PanZoom
- [ ] SelectionArea
- [ ] Rotatable
- [ ] RangeSlider
- [ ] Tree

## Bugs and verification

- [ ] fix #80 without weakening synchronous recursion limits
- [ ] Gallery integrated interaction scene and individual stories
- [ ] pointer/keyboard/accessibility/RTL/theme/lifecycle/virtualization matrix
- [ ] release benchmark proves pointer hot paths do not execute Rhai

## Explicit exclusions

DockLayout, OS/file drag, cross-window drag, 3D and compatibility aliases are outside 0.1.8.
title: 0.1.8: unify the Interaction Runtime before adding direct-manipulation components
Retained callbacks inherit the capture-time call level, so chaining `start_task` from a task callback hits `Stack overflow` after ~13 hops
